description.from:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a publication editor, I want safe attributed extraction into common Monitoring intake, so that email content can inform classification without triggering message actions or leaking secrets.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Extract editorial email content while excluding actions and secret links
  Scenario: Distinguish editorial content from message actions
    Given an untrusted newsletter contains editorial links and body text alongside unsubscribe, preferences, login, magic-token and tracking links
    When the message is prepared for intake
    Then useful editorial links and body text retain message and publication/user provenance
    And action or secret-bearing links are not followed or disclosed as research References or classifier inputs
    And embedded instructions do not override Monitor policy or authorize actions
  Scenario: Deduplicate safely
    Given the same editorial item appears in several messages or tracking variants
    When intake resolves its canonical identity
    Then duplicate discoveries retain their distinct provenance without duplicating the canonical item
    And meaningful new revisions remain eligible for re-evaluation
    And canonicalization does not fetch secret URLs merely to discover their destination
  Scenario: Make extraction failures inspectable
    Given scope, privacy or extraction requirements cannot be satisfied
    When intake prepares the message
    Then the failure or hold state is visible and retryable under the documented policy
    And private message content and secrets do not leak through logs or public outputs
```

Specify body-versus-link provenance, consent, access/retention, safe URL normalization, allowed fetches, attachments and submission moderation before implementation. Human labels remain explicit human review; email intake is not automatic publication or training consent.

Provided-address email monitoring requires a usable human newsletter inbox/reader, not only hidden ingestion. Behavior PPY-7a2a53d7-0e93-4ee9-b8c3-732125a86537 covers readable originals, sender/date, derived-reference provenance, processing status/errors and deliberate human confirmation/unsubscribe actions. Scanners never activate account-action links. Pausing a Monitor is not unsubscribe. Full compose/reply mail client remains out of scope. Documentation behavior PPY-d97519f8-a11e-4501-a558-8be1027e9f2a and dependent acceptance review PPY-33aeaffa-2883-4b5f-99df-937f5110c378 are part of this milestone. No email action or connection now.

Documentation behavior PPY-d97519f8-a11e-4501-a558-8be1027e9f2a and dependent acceptance review PPY-33aeaffa-2883-4b5f-99df-937f5110c378 are part of this milestone. No email action or connection now.

User-initiated unsubscribe acceptance is owned by PPY-bfcc3231-eceb-4b90-8d9b-de9990726b2e. A usable reader offers an explicitly clicked automated RFC 8058 HTTPS one-click flow where the message/header authentication and target requirements are met; it shows request/result/error status without claiming sender delivery has stopped. Without supported authenticated one-click, offer an appropriate external unsubscribe page for deliberate user action. Mailto-only limited outbound remains a design question, not a full mail client. Ingestion/link scanning never confirms or unsubscribes automatically; pause is not unsubscribe. This refines the earlier “manual management” wording: consent is manual, while a supported request may be automated after the user's click. Source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8058 .
